subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory contract, by memory-wiki as the knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new memory plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: Current source shows the gap, but choosing durable schema, conflict semantics, provenance requirements, and operator review UX is a product and ownership decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before implementation.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat structured claims, contradictions, and evidence as memory-wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core focused on files, search, promotion, and dreaming.

options.title: Defer the resolver
options.body: Keep the current Markdown, promotion, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before committing to a durable write API.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core or a new active-memory SDK seam as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent GitHub path history shows steipete across memory docs, memory-core, memory-host schema, and memory-wiki normalization work, making them the best available owner for the boundary decision.
